quest.title: For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...
quest.description: Sometimes, the best way to deal with schemes is by brutal force — a knot that cannot be undone can be ripped apart.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.title: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...

talks.objective: Go to the location mentioned in the Fatui's documents

dialogues.speaker: Investigate
dialogues.text: (Scattered, messy footprints both deep and shallow mark the area. There are even signs of a person tumbling across the sands... It is apparent that someone ran for their lives not long ago, leaving these footprints behind.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... What a mess of footprints... It looks... terrifying... Let's just get going.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Relax, there's nothing scary here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's exactly what makes this place creepy...

dialogues.speaker: Investigate
dialogues.text: (A smashed crate, with traces suggesting that it once contained something that was alive... But whatever it was, it is now free.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, the smell... This isn't good...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's not stay here. There are other signs ahead that might lead us to Jeht's location!

dialogues.speaker: Investigate
dialogues.text: (This tough canvas may once have been a part of a Fatui banner or tent. It's been torn apart to the point where you cannot discern its shape.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's like a cyclone passed through...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: *cough*... Look upon us... The Tanit... ruined... by a single traitor...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: My... tribe... my kin... my Eternal Oasis...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Say goodbye to them, while you still have time for some final words.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Why! ...I once... loved you so much... Why did you... betray me... and the Tanit...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Why? Because you're evil and I'm not. I see no reason why I must explain myself to you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright... Babel, let me tell you...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #It's because {NICKNAME} is {M#my best friend.}{F#my best friend!}

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #You wanted to get rid of {M#him}{F#her}, but I refused to be part of it, and so you decided to get rid of me too.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: No, you're more despicable than that... You wanted to pit us against each other!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Only then did I realize that you are no "Prophetess," nor do you deserve to be favored by the Queen of All Oases.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You're just a despicable schemer.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: You're... the foolish one... *cough* An outsider... You did all this, for an outsider!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I... We're your real family! You've destroyed everything. You destroyed... the hopes of the Tanit... the hopes of all the tribes who wander... amidst the gilded sands!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Stop bigging yourself up. I just pushed your tiny sand dune over, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Really, I'm the one with the questions here! What kind of mother would force her daughter to kill {M#her friend}{F#someone she cherishes}, anyway? Answer me!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Some family you are — you tried to take my life! Abyss take your idiotic dream of being a prophetess. Well, someone might fulfill it in your stead... But I'm sure they'll keep their hands cleaner than you did.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Haha... Hahaha... But I've already sent scouts to inform all the tribes of... your betrayal...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Soon, it'll be known... that you're a traitor who tarnished her family's name... *cough*... all across the vast desert... Very soon...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: No one will ever accept you again... Never again... will you find a safe place to lay your head...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...When did you do that?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: *cough*...! Haha... Right before... you came back...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you've always wanted us dead, then.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But you said before that you wanted to give me a chance to repent... Was that also a lie?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I thought... you'd soften... it'd make it easier to get rid of you...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You disgust me. All of you.

talks.objective: Chase the sounds to their source

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: *huff* *huff* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's her — that's Jeht! Is she injured?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Bleda... Gwaffah... Izder... Meddur... Teyya...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Uzad... Tafreh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are those... names?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #You're here, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Sorry, I might have lost my head a little back there... And sorry for getting caught as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not important! Are you hurt? Is it serious?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Come here. I've something to tell you two.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...Tell me, that you still remember my mother's name? If so... prove it with your sword.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Tell me, straight to my face, that you aren't despicable traitors — and then prove it!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I am calm. Draw your sword!

choices.text: I'm not a traitor. What happened to you?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: If you're not a traitor, you'll prove it with your sword.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: *huff* *huff* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now then. Let's talk.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I won't hurt you. Please, trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Whatever, I'm done with this. First, it was Azariq, and now it's you... *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Calm down. We were all deceived.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{M#He's}{F#She's} right! You said that the Matriarch asked you to hunt us down because we betrayed the tribe, but y'know what? That's the exact same mission she gave us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't believe you'd betray us, so we were trying to find you and figure things out.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I didn't betray the tribe, nor do I have any reason to do so.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Matriarch Babel has witnesses on her side: Yuften saw you deal with the northerners, and Masseira saw you moving around their camp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? No way! She also told us... that you were spotted colluding with enemies of the tribe!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So, why did they say you betrayed us? What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh... Paimon wishes we knew... Anyway, calm down and let us explain!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If it's Babel's design to pit us against each other...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will they defend us or the Matriarch?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Think about it, Jeht! Who do you trust more? Us or them?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Quiet down, would you, Paimon? This whole thing doesn't make any sense...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... You finally put your weapons down. Let's not draw 'em again, shall we? You gave Paimon quite a fright...
Don't be so optimistic yet, little one... She could still use her blades.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Nayram, Rezki! Why are you here? I can handle things alone here. There's no need for you to pitch in.

dialogues.speaker: Nayram
dialogues.text: Uh-huh, I can tell you're doing pretty well, Jeht... That's why Rezki and I are both needed to deal with the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Rezki
dialogues.text: ...And there's also this little Jinni.

dialogues.speaker: Nayram
dialogues.text: Oh, the little Jinni. I'm quite fond of her. Let's spare her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Rezki
dialogues.text: ...Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Wait, have... have you also betrayed the Tanit?

dialogues.speaker: Nayram
dialogues.text: No, on the contrary, we're here to deal with traitors.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I see.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are they?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: That's not important. They used to be good people.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Nayram, Rezki, it was a pleasure being your family. Now, forgive me.

dialogues.speaker: Rezki
dialogues.text: Alright. Let's do this.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Matriarch Babel sent them... What do you think they will do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You should take a look at this...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So, she set the trap up long ago, and was just waiting for us to walk right into it?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Wait... Why didn't you... show me this earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We would've, but you didn't give us a chance to speak before drawing your weapons, and you wouldn't listen to reason either!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Um... *sigh* I'm sorry. Thank goodness you're alright...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Regardless, I have to get to the bottom of this. I need answers from her.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Ugh... Ow, ow...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We still have time. You should rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup yup, there's no need to rush it. We can return any time, while Babel has to wait for us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon's right. The initiative is on our side now.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#Mm, you're right. I'm sorry that I didn't trust you...}{F#The initiative, huh...? Hmm...}

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, Jeht, show us your wounds already. We'll help bandage you up!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: My wounds? Where? Pfft... That's right. They're everywhere! ...Seriously though, I can keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't try to downplay it. Let us have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#*sigh*... Okay. Sorry...}{F#Mm... Okay...}

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And so, you all decide to rest briefly and start a campfire...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
#{M#After carefully tending to Jeht's wounds, you get some rest together with her by the campfire.
Though no words are spoken, you both know what must happen next.}{F#After carefully tending to Jeht's wound, you get some rest together with her by the campfire...
Jeht sleeps peacefully by your side. The mixed odors of blood, sweat, and burning poplar branches cannot fully mask the scent of spices she carries.
Light snoring and raving nonsense intertwine in her dreams — she must truly be tired.
Even without speaking to one another, you both know what must happen once she awakes.}

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...Let's go. Let's find Babel and have her explain everything to us.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: ...It's you, Jeht! You're... You're back.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yes, we're back, alive. I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: It does my heart good to see you return safely... You must be in need of some rest. Come, let me see what I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I don't need to rest. I need answers.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Why did you lure me into the northerners' trap? Why did you send other members of the tribe to kill me? Why do you want me dead?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Calm down. Listen, Jeht...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Do you remember what I told you? Of how the Eternal Oasis is the Tanit's hope, and how it will bestow a prosperous homeland upon us? It is exactly for this cause that you pledged your loyalty to me, no?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Now that the door to the Oasis is open to the Tanit, we must keep it a secret from outsiders...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: We must ensure that the Tanit are and will remain the most beloved children of the Queen of All Oases... Only thus can we guide the other wandering desert tribes to gather by the Oasis.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: And when they do... Just think about it — faith will allow us to reunite the scattered peoples of the desert and their resources.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Under the guidance of the Queen of All Oases, we will rebuild a nation of oases in this desert with our own two hands, and once that is done, none of us shall ever have to bow to those city ilk ever again.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: We will be able to build our own palaces, develop an academic system unique to us. We shall even challenge that god who's naught but a mere caged bird!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Of all those things that I told you, have you not listened to a single word?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: And I told you that it was impossible! The Queen of All Oases is long gone. She's not in the Oasis, and there's no way we can resurrect her!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Preposterous! Even as my most beloved daughter, how dare you spout such nonsense!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Whether she is alive or dead, whether she can or cannot be resurrected... As long as the Eternal Oasis is under my control, all such things will be mine to decide.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I shall be the sole Prophetess of the slumbering goddess, the Tanit's law shall be divine edict, and the prosperity of the Tanit shall be the pre-ordinance of her divine oracles.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: But before all that comes true, Jeht... It's not yet too late to repent. You are my most beloved daughter, and I wish to set you back on the right path.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I—I don't understand. What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I've made my point clear: The one and only oracle demands absolute obedience. The only ones who haven't been blinded by the truth of the Oasis are you and your outsider friend.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: And this outsider remains the Master of the Jinni. Though the Jinni herself has long gone silent, we can gain control over her as long as we get rid of her master.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Of the two of us, it is I who respects her ancient wisdom and the power to rebuild the Oasis. It is more fitting, therefore, that we gain mastery over the Jinni.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's that supposed to mean?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: You dodged the question last time... and that is understandable.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: But today, you must make a choice: Tanit, your home, or this outsider, this friend of yours.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait. Are you saying that you discussed how to get rid of me previously?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Yes... But I refused. {M#I mean, come on! You're my friend, after all.}{F#I mean, how could I? You're so important to me.}

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: #I'm sorry, my child, but sacrifice is necessary... I shall not let {M#his}{F#her} noble blood be shed in vain. On that, you can have absolute faith in me.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: As for you, Jeht, you will become my successor, and one day, you will be the Tanit's new Matriarch and Nabu Malikata's Prophetess.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Please, consider my offer. The future of our home lies in your hands, my daughter. Merely ask it of me, and I will give you time and one more chance.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: There's no need. I've made up my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, you sure you don't want more time? This situation's, like, super tense!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Babel, I appreciate your help all throughout this time... Though I'm well aware of the fact that I'm the daughter of a traitor and an outsider.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I couldn't be more grateful... for your arrangements.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...The things that I've done for you, the voices I've silenced for you, the elders who disappeared...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Elder Bleda, the one who liked crocodiles... surely you remember him? He treated you like his daughter, and he doted on me as well... That's why I could plunge a poisoned dagger into his chest.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Elder Gwaffah was such an eyesore to you, and you were that to him, too. And sadly, it was me in the end with a Sumpter Beast's jawbone. Again, and again, and again, and again...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: That was the first time I had ever been scared to tears. I was so afraid of myself. I still remember how you wiped my tears away...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on... Are you saying...!? ... How could that be...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Wait. Why are you bringing this up? Why do you have to bring this up in front of them?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Ah, and there was also Elder Teyya. She was young and beautiful, and she was the head of the hunting party... a more capable competitor than you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: She thought I adored her, but I was loyal to you, for I believed that you alone were my true family. I believed that you could wipe my tears away once more and give me a home.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So I made her disappear in the desert...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: And what is the point of this meaningless talk?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You are the "sole oracle of the goddess" and my "mother." Why should there be any secrets between us?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: If you wish to hear more, I can spell every one of my deeds out to you, and to all the Tanit.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Everything I've done for you, my mother, and for this family.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #I've done enough, and I'm fed up with it. I won't betray {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: You're mad... How dare you slander me, your Matriarch! You've forgotten your mother's name! Silence — I bid you be silent now, before it is too late!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: My mother's name is Ufairah — Ufairah Hindi. She was an honest person.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Ah, so it was true, then. The traitor's daughter could never be anything but a half-grown mongrel... just like her father.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Jebrael and that outsider woman have already paid the price for the unforgivable things they did, and now, their daughter repeats their errors. I should've seen that coming!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Ufairah Hindi, that's her name... And it will be mine as well.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Traitor! All my teachings were for nothing! May the desert mark your treachery!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Enough! My kin, you know what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: She has angered... and saddened me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh...! Hold on! Don't get so worked up! Didn't you just say that you see Jeht as your daughter... Besides, {NICKNAME} has helped you so many times...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Anyway, there's still gotta be a way to come to an understanding, right?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Paimon, hide yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Keep your eyes closed... and don't dirty your white clothes.

talks.objective: Defeat the forces of the Tanit Tribe
Defeat the forces of the Tanit Tribe
Defeat the forces of the Tanit Tribe
Witness the fall of the Tanit
Follow Jeht out of this place

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can always trust us, Jeht!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I know... It's just that I'm left with nowhere to return to again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But put another way, you're now free to call anywhere you wish home.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Pfft, if it were me back then, I'd have thought that you were mocking me! *sigh* But you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You're right... Now, I'm the head of my own house.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I'm no longer a servant bound by the name "Tanit." I'm now the master of the name "Jeht."

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I've reclaimed my mother's name... I'm free. Perhaps "Jeht" will also become the name of a new clan someday... Maybe? I dunno.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: My mother's name gives me pride, and my father's name also holds many memories for me. As long as I remember them, even in this barren desert... Will that not be the home I was seeking all along?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now, "home" need not be a cause of anxiety for you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Uh... You know what? Actually, I'd love to go on more adventures with you... Haha, never mind that. You must've had enough of me after all the dangerous situations I put you in...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But... I can tell that you have your own journey ahead, a travail of greater solitude and a far grander objective, both of which are beyond what I can bear or imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: As for me, I've also set myself on a certain path. You've seen it already... It's not gonna be a peaceful one. And I won't drag you down with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...C'mon, Jeht, you're not "dragging us down" or anything...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Anyway, if you ever feel tired or want to take a breather... I believe that our paths will converge one day.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: At that time, I might even invite you to go on a crazy adventure with me again.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Phew... I've done enough talking... It's time to leave. There's nothing left here but heartbreak.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
#{M#You hug Jeht before parting ways with her in the desert.
She holds you tightly, and you notice that she seems to be holding back sobs...
However, she quickly draws back and rubs her wet eyes before smiling broadly at you once more.}{F#You hug Jeht before parting ways with her in the desert.
She holds you tightly, almost as if afraid that a blinding sandstorm would sweep you away. You notice that she seems to be holding back sobs...
Then she pushes you away lightly and rubs her wet eyes before smiling broadly at you once more.}

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "May we meet again under a lovelier sun," she says.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jeht turns away and leaves.\nYou see Benben, only now emerging out of the ruined camp, hurry to catch up with Jeht.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Go ahead! I take your bullets! You think you kill me with bullets? I take your bullets! Go ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's Jeht. It's like... she's gone mad with fury...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You scum! Come back! I'll rip out your livers. I'll grill you alive. I will chomp on your bones!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Does she even know what she's saying?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Capture me alive? Capture me alive, will you? Oh, you'll capture me alright — once I've bled my last drop of blood on these sands! Come on!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... There wouldn't be anyone alive to capture in that case...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: There she is... probably waiting for Nayram and Rezki.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who are they again...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Her assassins. We've fought them already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No sign of the Fatui... Hmm, but look at the things scattered around this place. Someone must've been here before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht... Jeht, where are you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht! Look, is that Jeht over there? Quick, let's go!
